s1.title: Cultural traces
s1.body: The Hitotoki Collective leaves cultural traces — signposts for the forecestors who will navigate their own paths in their own times. Each trace is anchored in a multi-dimensional creative space where the moment itself is quintessential.

s2.title: The moment is quintessential
s2.body: Painting, music, film, photography and movement converge in live multimedia performances staged in sacred places, such as the ancient temples of Kyoto, where time opens onto a primordial timelessness. Nothing is rehearsed into permanence; what matters is what happens once.

s3.title: A counter-intuitive economics
s3.body: The Collective takes a counter-intuitive approach to the economics of culture. Funded by sponsors in tune with the spirit of the project, the analog fruits of each performance are offered freely to the guardians of the places that receive them.

s4.title: The guardians
s4.body: Each offering is made as a mark of profound and joyful respect — yet it would be remiss not to declare a second motive: the belief that these guardians offer the best assurance that the signposts will withstand the vicissitudes of history.

performances.title: Traces
performances.lede: Each performance is recorded in the archive as a trace — numbered, placed, and given away. Two traces have been laid so far, both in Kyoto.

performance.settingBody: Staged within a sacred precinct of Kyoto, among structures that have kept their vigil for centuries. Time there opens onto a primordial timelessness, and the performance enters it for the span of a single evening.
performance.elementsLine: Painting, music, film, photography and movement — converging live, unrepeatable, in a single moment.
performance.offeringBody: The analog fruits of this performance were offered freely to the guardians of the place, as a mark of profound and joyful respect — and in the belief that such guardians offer the best assurance that the trace will withstand the vicissitudes of history.
performance.archiveNote: Moving-image documentation of this trace is held in the Collective's archive.

01-jp-kyo.p0: An ink painting of a dragon, rearing in a storm of brushstrokes, standing on canvas in a Kyoto temple garden beside a pond and a stone lantern.
01-jp-kyo.p1: The dragon painting standing on a black cloth at the pond's edge, surrounded by brushes, an ink vessel and the garden's pines.

02-jp-kyo.p0: A large painting of a fox in vermilion and black ink, flanked by calligraphy, hung above the wooden steps of a temple hall; the artist sits below it in dark robes.

patronage.title: Sponsors and guardians
patronage.lede: The Collective is funded by sponsors in tune with the spirit of the project. The fruits of each performance are not sold; they are given.
patronage.sponsorsBody: Sponsorship is an act of alignment rather than exchange. Sponsors make each performance possible and, in doing so, enter the lineage of the trace it leaves behind.
patronage.guardiansBody: The guardians — keepers of the sacred places that host each performance — receive the offerings and carry them forward through time, as they have carried so much else.
patronage.correspondenceBody: Introductions travel by word of mouth, through the sponsors and guardians of the Collective. If the spirit of the project speaks to you, you will find your way to us.

footer.origin: Born in Switzerland, bred in Japan, coming of age everywhere.
